newsitem.title: USA: BPA offers 300 MW off-peak power for Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: BPA offers 300 MW off-peak power for Tuesday.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) offered up to 300 megawatts (MW) of off-peak electricity for delivery Tuesday at $20.75 per megawatt hour (MWh), the federal agency said Monday.
BPA did not offer any peak power for Tuesday.
Off-peak power for Tuesday the hours 0600 and 2300 PST in the Northwest and the California Oregon Border (COB) was offered at $21.00 per MWh, BPA said.
Light load power for Monday delivery was offered Friday at $22.25/MWh and at $23.00 for the Northwest and COB.
Peak power for Monday delivery had been offered last week at $31.50 per MWh, and at $32.00 in the Northwest and $32.75 at COB.
Also for Tuesday delivery, Bonneville said it was offering light-load electricity, with a 500 MW limit, at $17.75 per MWh, with prices set at $18.50 for the Northwest and COB.
Non-firm power from hours one to five and 24 on Tuesday, again with a 300 MW limit, was being offered at $18.25 and at $19.00 per MWh in the Northwest and COB, BPA said.
